messages.author: edf3f9a83bf3101c
messages.subject: Shiny Concurrent Access & Feature List
parts:
I have a R&D team that has been researching Shiny for some web based analytical simulators they hope to develop and deploy.  They have run into some issues with concurrent access from their web simulator.  Can you help me to understand and appreciate
 
1) Is concurrency limitation an issue with the beta of Shiny, or is this a limitation with R in general?
         If Shiny, will the upcoming commercial version address this?
2) What are the differences between the beta today and the upcoming commercial version?  is there a link to see the upcoming features and/or history of the releases?
3) Once the commercial version is available, what will it cost and what will the support model look like?
 
Many Thanks!!
Michael

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Concurrent Access & Feature List
parts: On Fri, May 24, 2013 at 8:50 AM, Michael Sevast <michael...@gmail.com> wrote:

1) Is concurrency limitation an issue with the beta of Shiny, or is this a limitation with R in general?
         If Shiny, will the upcoming commercial version address this?
The issue is that R does not support concurrent execution. We plan to address this in the commercial version of Shiny by launching multiple R processes, up to 1 per user.
2) What are the differences between the beta today and the upcoming commercial version?  is there a link to see the upcoming features and/or history of the releases?

There isn't a public feature list. We intend to release a very early version of the commercial server in late June with simple authentication features, multiple R processes per app, and removal of the requirement to run the server as root. (That last feature will be upstreamed to the open source version as well.) Additional features will be in the final 1.0 release, mostly around security, monitoring, and scaling.
3) Once the commercial version is available, what will it cost and what will the support model look like?

We don't intend to charge for the preview version. Pricing for the final version and support are both TBD. If you want to contact me off-list I'd be very interested to hear what your needs and budget are.

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Concurrent Access & Feature List
parts:
Hi Michael.

(Thanks for your patience on this. We're hoping to get this Enterprise version out to users ASAP.)

The good news is that 30 concurrent users will be a very moderate number in terms of the scale we want Shiny Server to be able to handle, so I don't think you'll end up having to push any boundaries in the software there. My suspicion is that the average use case's hardware requirements will be dominated by the Shiny application you're trying to run, rather than anything in Shiny Server. So you should be able to get a pretty accurate benchmark of the resources you'll need by running the Shiny App you've developed locally on your hardware and monitoring things like RAM and CPU utilization of the R process. Keep in mind that R is single-threaded, meaning that one simulation can run on one R process at a time. So to facilitate 30 simultaneous Shiny users, you'd be looking at running 30 of these separate R processes.

(To be clear for others who may read this message: not every use case demands a separate process per concurrent user. For instance, any of the examples that are bundled with Shiny or are discussed in the tutorial are very "lightweight" regarding computation, and can successfully handle dozens of users with only a single R process. This one-process-per-concurrent-user model only applies in computationally heavy scenarios such as running these lengthy simulations.)

Hope that helps!
Jeff
